# How small business owners can prepare for a successful 2027


November 23, 2026


Business Banking


Media and Press


Small Business


-
-
-
-


Wars, tariffs, election year changes, interest rates. Headlines give small business owners plenty to consider heading into 2027, but when Stephen Ball, Head of Business Banking at Byline Bank, talks with owners across Chicagoland, the concerns he hears most are far more ordinary: how to find good employees, manage cash flow, keep up with expenses, and protect against fraud.


In a new article in the Daily Herald, Stephen shares how the most successful local businesses are planning for the year ahead:


- **Build resilience:** Review expenses and pricing, and keep cash reserves for the unexpected.


- **Invest in your people:** Respect, flexibility and a relationship-based approach help keep good employees.


- **Let the business case drive financing:** Big purchases should hinge on your business model, not the rate environment.


- **Grow sustainably:** Strong demand is great, but diversify and build your balance sheet before taking on larger commitments.


- **Make technology work for you:** Start with a specific need, not the latest tool.


His takeaway: owners who understand their market, take care of their employees, keep their finances in order and make thoughtful decisions about growth will be better positioned for whatever comes next.


Read the full article in the Daily Herald:


[Keep your eye on the business, not the headlines](https://www.dailyherald.com/2026/11/20/small-business-outlook-2027-keep-your-eye-on-the-business-not-the-headlines/)
